reply_text:
I found the quoted words on the page, character for character. My admission reading is **borderline**. Part 2 is the main doubt, and part 1 is less certain than it looks.

**The page.** The Sina Finance page opened. It reprints the 暗涌Waves (36Kr) interview "疯狂的幻方：一家隐形AI巨头的大模型之路", by 于丽丽, dated 2023年05月24日 18:04. The quote is in Liang Wenfeng's own answer, in printed question-and-answer form. He is answering the interviewer's point that a startup entering after the big companies is "not a good time". Note that this is a reprint on a news portal, not 36Kr's own page. The text is still the printed Q&A, so I would not call it coverage only.

**Part 1 (role).** Borderline. The article says that "in May" High-Flyer named its new independent LLM organisation 深度求索 (DeepSeek), and Liang answers as its founder-leader. But DeepSeek was not yet registered as a company. Its incorporation is usually given as July 2023, which I know from memory and did not check here. The role history only says "2023". High-Flyer itself was a quant fund, not yet a model builder. I lean towards counting the role, but a person should rule on it.

**Part 2 (looks forward, about AI).** Borderline. He says big companies and startups will all have built their own large language models by next year at the latest. That is about AI models being made, but in context it is a point about competition: no one can build a crushing technical lead. It says nothing about what the AI will do or about its deployment. It sits close to the industry and business forecasts the rule keeps out. Its test would also be vague, since "big companies and startups" is not a defined set. The rule says a truly borderline case stays out and is logged as borderline.

**Part 3 (date).** Passes. "最晚明年" (by next year at the latest) gives 2024.

**Part 4 (primary source).** Passes, because the source is a printed Q&A.

**Recorded?** No. This is not the same claim as the one on file (2024-07-22, AGI in two, five or ten years).
